actors: the Bell Telephone Companies (as later reported)

event: Experimental underground cables laid a short distance alongside a Massachusetts railroad track, 'with small results'
notes: Earliest engineering act the registrant attributes to itself in the window

event: Cables laid at Boston by the American Bell Telephone Company, longest 1,500 feet; users could not talk beyond the suburbs; later turned over to the New England Company
actors: American Bell Telephone Company (P1 lineage) and the New England Company
evidence_class: CONTEMPORANEOUS OBSERVATION (1887 print, plus a third company's letter)
notes: Cross-carrier with S4449 l.1418-1426. The 1887 letter prints 'April, 1853' for the April 1883 Clark cables - an OCR defect, not a second event

event: First Paterson underground cable laid in New York completed: 100 conductors, 1,965 feet
notes: THE 1885 DECOY: a grep for 1885 in this 1887 document returns cable completions, not an incorporation

event: Brooks system at the Spring Street Exchange completed: 400 wires in an oil-filled iron pipe, 2,449 feet
notes: Subsequently failed on water ingress and was re-drawn - see the failures register

event: INCORPORATED under the laws of the State of New York
evidence_class: RESTATED (a 1994 filing reciting 1885; no in-window carrier)
notes: The single filed sentence for the origin of the historic registrant. State is NEW YORK, not New Jersey

event: Introduction of the twisted-pair underground conductor, which the company says meant the abandonment of the entire underground plant of the Bell System
notes: No held byte prices the abandoned plant; the dossier does not convert this into an impairment figure

event: Dorsett conduit cables on Sixth Avenue (21st-58th Streets) completed: 300 conductors, all working
notes: Insulation 500-1,000 megohms per mile; the report prefers these to the Brooklyn cable and cannot say why

event: Three-day conference on telephone cables held at the office of the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, 18 Courtlandt Street; proceedings printed, not published
actors: P2 with American Bell, Western Electric, New York & New Jersey Telephone, Metropolitan Telephone & Telegraph
notes: The earliest held document showing the registrant acting. Nine named participants, five companies

event: Expiration of the Bell patents; the held corpus's only dated statement of the opening of competition
actors: the art and every independent company
evidence_class: CONTEMPORANEOUS OBSERVATION by an interested third party
notes: P2's own print never states it. This is the one in-window date that reorganises the stage's competition story

event: Independent companies entering the field (1895 to 1900); and the first column of three of the registrant's own statistical series
actors: the independents; P2's associated operating companies
notes: No carrier exists for a 1895 transcontinental experiment; 1895 in the company print is arithmetic, not an event

event: The transfer of the Bell System parentage from American Bell to the registrant
evidence_class: UNKNOWN - no carrier in held bytes
notes: The most consequential brand-lineage event in the window and the one the corpus cannot reach; G-3

event: Pupin loading coils and other improvements permit a loaded suburban cable between New York and Newark
The Chicago & Milwaukee Telegraph Line goes into receivership (1905) and is sold (1907) to the Chicago and Wisconsin Telephone Companies in connection with the registrant
actors: another company's failure absorbed by P2
evidence_class: FACT (appendix reprint inside the registrant's own print)
notes: The corpus's first incurred commercial failure and first documented acquisition by this registrant - and neither is a failure of P4, which did not exist

event: A loaded cable 90 miles long operated between New York and Philadelphia, usable in the then state of the art only between those cities
notes: The 150,000,000 of 4 per cent convertible bonds of 1906 were 96.9 per cent converted by 1913-12-31

event: A cable capable of satisfactory conversation between Washington and Boston designed
notes: A design claim, not a demonstration; the demonstration follows in 1912-1913

event: First underground talk New York-Washington, 'the longest distance underground yet achieved'; section Washington-Philadelphia laid
Act of Congress directs the Interstate Commerce Commission to value the property of common carriers, which the report states includes all the principal telephone companies
actors: the ICC; P2 and every peer
notes: The regulatory mechanism that made the registrant's valuation argument a live issue at the stage edge

event: Satisfactory conversation by underground wire achieved Boston-Washington, through cable of several generations; New York-Denver line studied and its rearrangement planned
notes: The strongest validated achievement inside Stage 1; 47 per cent of the cable in the line was of short-haul types

event: Five-point course of action accepted by the Directors and signed by N. C. Kingsbury, Vice President; acknowledged the same day by Attorney General J. C. McReynolds, with the President's note printed
actors: P2, the Department of Justice, the Presidency
notes: Disposes of Western Union stock; ends acquisition of competing telephone companies; opens toll interconnection on stated terms

event: Year-end position: 8,133,017 system stations, 55,983 shareholders, capital stock 344,616,300, total assets 655,956,307.97
notes: Last dated position the corpus can certify; the stage edge itself carries only a plan

event: Director Henry P. Davison resigned, per the footnote on the officers' page of the FY1913 report
notes: The only board movement printed inside the window

event: 'with the completion of the line to the Pacific Coast in 1915, commercial communication will be dependable and practicable' - a projection, and the only 1915 statement of the opening in held bytes
notes: Stage 1 closes on this line. Nothing in sources/ reports the event; transcontinental prints 0 times
